Memorial at the Former Synagogue Site in Jever

Memorial · Jever, Germany

The property at Große Wasserpfortstraße 19 is Jever's principal memorial site for the former Jewish community. A purpose-built synagogue completed in 1802 stood here before the community replaced it with a larger synagogue in 1880. Local perpetrators burned the 1880 building during the November pogrom on 10 November 1938, and the original structure no longer exists. A commercial building was erected on the gap in 1954; since 2014 it has housed the GröschlerHaus centre for Jewish and contemporary regional history. The mapped feature is therefore classified as a memorial at a destroyed synagogue site.
